Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T18:01:45Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is backed by real error responses at that proxy: over 17:01:45–18:40:45 its spans carry ~1,742 STATUS_CODE_ERROR entries (ingress ~1,371, 'router frontend egress' ~371) against ~34,530 STATUS_CODE_UNSET, and its own Envoy access log shows 'POST /api/checkout ... 504 UT response_timeout ... 15000' plus 'GET /api/data?... 500 - via_upstream'. Two distinct failure streams feed those errors. (1) Dominant, sustained: frontend-proxy's 504s are 15-second response timeouts on POST /api/checkout; the upstream frontend handler runs 89–97 s because checkout's 'orders publish' span blocks ~86–95 s and fails with 'circuit breaker is open' / 'kafka server: Request was for a topic or partition that does not exist on this broker'. Checkout's logs show Kafka metadata i/o timeouts to the kafka Service ClusterIP 100.71.78.255:9092, and both kafka broker pods log a single-node id/epoch conflict (STALE_BROKER_EPOCH, repeated AssignReplicasToDirsRequestData unexpected errors, endless __consumer_offsets CreateTopics retries) even though both pods are Running and Ready. The kafka Deployment runs 2 replicas against a single-voter KRaft config (KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS=1@kafka:9093, advertised listener kafka:9092, no per-replica node id), which is the deepest supported cause. (2) Transient: 18:20–18:28 a burst of /api/data 500s matched frontend 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' error spans (~0.47–0.6/s), starting right after ad's container was OOMKilled at 18:19:26 (exit 137, limit 450Mi); the ad-side mechanism could not be confirmed because Jaeger only held traces for 18:17:49–18:19:19. The alert rule itself is not loaded in the queried Prometheus, so its expression and the 'current: 1.6' value could not be verified.

claims.text: otel-demo/frontend-proxy has exactly two span operations, 'ingress' (server) and 'router frontend egress' (client), and both carry error status: whole-window increase of STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans is ~1,742 (ingress ~1,371.1, 'router frontend egress' ~371.5) versus ~34,529.8 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans. These are span counts, not request counts.

frontend-proxy's error rate was mixed, not monotonic: 'ingress' ERROR spans ran ~0.24–0.38/s from 18:03:45 through 18:19:45, rose to ~0.81–0.88/s at 18:21:45–18:27:45 and fell back to ~0.31–0.39/s at 18:29:45–18:31:45; 'router frontend egress' ERROR spans were 0 until 18:21:45, then ~0.44–0.60/s, then 0 after 18:27:45.

frontend-proxy ingress spans observed in the supplied trace sample are 504s: error=true, http.status_code="504", otel.status_code=ERROR, duration ~15,001,929 us, each paired with a 'router frontend egress' span of ~15,001,683 us carrying error="true" http.status_code="0".

frontend-proxy's own access log shows the failing responses: 13 lines of 'POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 504 UT response_timeout ... 15000/15001 ms' between 18:10:00.130 and 18:10:19.522, and 'GET /api/data?contextKeys=books HTTP/1.1" 500 - via_upstream ... 21' at 18:24:23.769 alongside further 504 checkout timeouts at 18:24:26.962 and 18:24:28.038.

A single trace (f18dd56ad5afb108674a31c6c7770ed1) shows the causal ordering: load-generator 'user_checkout_single' 15.44 s -> load-generator POST 15.00 s http 504 ERROR -> frontend-proxy ingress 504 -> frontend-proxy egress 15.00 s -> frontend 'POST /api/checkout' 89.09 s (http 200) -> frontend grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 89.08 s -> checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 89.08 s -> checkout 'orders publish' 88.87 s ERROR with otel.status_description 'circuit breaker is open'. Cart, product-catalog, currency, shipping/quote, payment and email sub-calls in the same trace completed in microseconds to ~100 ms.

checkout's only error operation is 'orders publish' (~862 ERROR spans over the window, 0 for every other checkout operation), and its error rate ran continuously at ~0.26–0.34/s from 18:03:45 to about 18:25:45. Error text on those spans includes 'circuit breaker is open' and 'kafka server: Request was for a topic or partition that does not exist on this broker'.

checkout pod logs state the Kafka failure directly: 'Failed to write message: circuit breaker is open', 'kafka: Failed to produce message to topic orders: circuit breaker is open', 'client/metadata got error from broker 1 while fetching metadata: read tcp 100.96.1.134:53048->100.71.78.255:9092: i/o timeout', 'Closed connection to broker kafka:9092' and 'client/brokers deregistered broker #1 at kafka:9092' (18:29:12–18:29:53).
100.71.78.255 is the otel-demo 'kafka' Service ClusterIP on port 9092, and checkout's pod IP is 100.96.1.134, so the i/o timeout is from the checkout pod to the Kafka Service endpoint.

Retrying.' and repeats '[QuorumController id=1] CreateTopics ... __consumer_offsets ... TOPIC_ALREADY_EXISTS' roughly every 100 ms; kafka-ff7884766-xclnk logs '[ControllerApis nodeId=1] Unexpected error handling request ... AssignReplicasToDirsRequestData(brokerId=1, brokerEpoch=10 ...)' and at 18:29:12 'CreateTopics ... CreatableTopic(name='orders' ...): TOPIC_ALREADY_EXISTS', i.e. the 'orders' topic exists in metadata while clients are told it does not exist on the broker.

The otel-demo 'kafka' Deployment is configured with replicas=2 and a single shared container env: KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS=1@kafka:9093 (the kafka Service name, not a per-pod address), KAFKA_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS=PLAINTEXT://kafka:9092, KAFKA_LISTENERS=PLAINTEXT://:9092,CONTROLLER://:9093, KAFKA_HEAP_OPTS=-Xmx400M -Xms400M, limits cpu 400m / memory 900Mi, and no per-replica node.id variable; both pods are Running with 0 restarts and the Deployment reports ready=2, updated=2, generation 1.

Other services showed no error-status span series in the window: only ad (~39.9), checkout (~862.1), fraud-detection (~2.0), frontend (~1,502.3), frontend-proxy (~1,742.6), recommendation (~4.1) appeared, with accounting and payment explicitly at 0; no error series was returned for cart, currency, email, product-catalog, quote, shipping, image-provider or flagd. fraud-detection and recommendation errors are only 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' spans, not tied by this evidence to the proxy's 504/500 responses.

All 21 otel-demo Deployments report ready replicas equal to their spec (including kafka ready=2), all 22 pods are Running, and only ad has a non-zero restart count (1); all five nodes are Ready with MemoryPressure=False, DiskPressure=False and PIDPressure=False and ~16 GiB allocatable memory each.

Primary hypothesis: the otel-demo 'kafka' Deployment is the origin of the sustained frontend-proxy errors. With replicas=2 sharing one single-voter KRaft configuration (KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS=1@kafka:9093 pointing at the load-balanced Service and no distinct node.id per pod), both broker pods operate as id 1 and fight over broker epochs (STALE_BROKER_EPOCH, unexpected AssignReplicasToDirsRequestData handling), so cluster metadata/leadership for topic 'orders' is inconsistent ('topic or partition that does not exist on this broker', metadata i/o timeouts). checkout's produce call therefore hangs ~86–95 s and trips 'circuit breaker is open', PlaceOrder runs ~89 s, and frontend-proxy's 15 s response timeout turns the request into a 504 — the error signal behind RequestErrorRate.

Secondary hypothesis (unresolved): the ad service's OOMKill and restart at 18:19:26 immediately preceded the 18:20–18:28 burst of frontend 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' errors and the matching 'GET /api/data ... 500' responses at frontend-proxy, with ad's memory limited to 450Mi. The ad-side mechanism (unavailable, slow, or returning errors) is not established because Jaeger held no traces for that interval and ad's GetAds/GetAds-server spans were not observable.

Rejected: frontend-proxy itself is not the origin. Its pod has restartCount=0, it kept serving (many 200/308 responses in the same log stream), and every failing entry is either '504 UT response_timeout' at the 15000 ms route timeout or a '500 - via_upstream' propagated from the frontend; the corresponding upstream spans show multi-second-to-90-second handler durations, so the proxy is reporting upstream slowness rather than failing on its own.

Rejected: node-level resource pressure does not explain the ad OOMKill or kafka slowness. All five nodes are Ready with MemoryPressure=False, DiskPressure=False, PIDPressure=False and roughly 16 GiB allocatable memory; the affected pods are spread across nodes i-07383de2f90cfeb17, i-0462024ad5561246c and i-0fcb81fcf54753a7d.

Kafka's surface state looks healthy: both kafka pods are Running and Ready, the Deployment reports ready=2/updated=2 with generation 1 and observedGeneration 1, restarts are 0, and the pods were created at 17:49:47Z. This is why the failure is not visible as a crash loop and why readiness cannot be used to clear kafka; the broker-internal logs show the conflict.

ad was not continuously failing: its logs at 18:19:21–18:19:23 show ordinary serving lines ('Non-targeted ad request received, preparing random response.', 'Targeted ad request received for [travel]'), so the OOMKill is a discrete restart event rather than a long outage seen in its own logs; the GetAds error interval cannot be attributed to ad from ad's own evidence.

Reconcile the kafka Deployment with its KRaft configuration: either scale otel-demo/kafka to 1 replica to match the single-voter quorum KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS=1@kafka:9093, or give each replica a distinct node.id and a real multi-voter quorum with per-pod advertised addresses; then restart the brokers and confirm that topic 'orders' has a live partition leader before re-testing checkout.

Treat the ad OOMKill as a separate item: inspect ad memory usage against its 450Mi limit (cpu limit 50m), add probes so a sick ad instance leaves the Service endpoints, and re-check whether GetAds failures disappear after a memory-limit adjustment.

Make the checkout path fail fast instead of hanging: align Envoy's 15 s route timeout with the checkout producer's publish/circuit-breaker timeout so a Kafka outage returns a fast 5xx instead of an 89–97 s handler that the proxy can only report as a timeout.

No change_history integration is available, so it cannot be determined whether kafka replicas=2 was a deliberate change or the initial install; all Deployments show generation 1 and all pods were created 17:49:46–17:49:48Z.

Whether topic 'orders' currently has a valid partition leader, and whether both kafka Service endpoints are selected by the 'kafka' Service, could not be verified (no topic or endpoint inspection was available).

Span-based counts are extrapolated increases over sampled traces and are not request counts; per-status-code request totals for frontend-proxy cannot be derived from the available labels (only service_name, span_name, status_code).

Verify kafka broker identity/quorum: check each broker's node.id and KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS, and list topic 'orders' partition leadership and ISR.

If the chart intends a single broker, set otel-demo/kafka replicas to 1 (or reconfigure per-pod node.id and quorum addresses), roll the brokers and re-run a checkout to confirm PlaceOrder latency returns to sub-second.
Review ad pod memory usage against the 450Mi limit and its 50m CPU limit; adjust limits and add readiness/liveness probes so a restarted ad instance is removed from Service endpoints.
Add alerting on pod restart/OOMKilled and on kafka broker-level errors (STALE_BROKER_EPOCH, under-replicated partitions) so the underlying instability is visible before proxy error-rate alerts fire.
